trap.wrong: "Build a direct integration from our order service to each partner's API."
trap.why: Each partner has different formats, reliability and protocols; direct coupling spreads partner quirks through core systems, and failures or format changes in one partner break your flows. Without reconciliation, missing messages go unnoticed.
trap.probe: An integration layer with canonical models, adapters per partner, durable queues, monitoring and reconciliation.
trap.say: "An integration layer translating each partner's format to a canonical model, with adapters per partner, durable queues and retries, raw message archives, per-partner monitoring, and reconciliation of what was sent and acknowledged against what partners report."

thesis: Partner integrations are unreliable, heterogeneous and slow to change. Isolate them behind an integration layer with a canonical internal model, per-partner adapters, durable asynchronous delivery, raw message archives, monitoring per partner, and regular reconciliation to catch what fell through the cracks.
pitch: Core services publish and consume canonical events like ShipmentCreated or InventoryUpdated. An integration layer has an adapter per partner that translates to and from their format: REST, SOAP, SFTP files, EDI documents. Outbound messages go through durable queues with retries and backoff, idempotency keys where partners support them, and per-partner rate limits. Inbound messages are archived raw before parsing, so failures can be replayed after fixing a parser, and parsing errors go to a dead-letter queue with alerts. Each partner has dashboards for volume, latency, error rate and acknowledgement gaps, because a partner silently sending nothing looks like a quiet day. Reconciliation compares our records with partner reports: shipments we sent versus those they acknowledged, inventory we think a supplier has versus their file. And I'd version adapters independently, test them against recorded partner messages, and onboard new partners through configuration where formats are standard.

points.d: Core systems speak one data model; partner formats never leak into them.
Translation, protocol handling and partner quirks isolated and independently deployable.
Queues with retries, backoff, idempotency and per-partner rate limits.
Store original inbound and outbound payloads for audit, debugging and replay after parser fixes.
Volume, error rates, latency and missing acknowledgements, with alerts for silence as well as errors.
Periodic comparison of what each side believes happened, with exception handling.
Recorded partner messages as test fixtures, catching breaking changes before deploys.

decision: A dedicated integration layer (or integration platform) for all partners, canonical events internally, and reconciliation as a standard control for every partner relationship.
numbers: Monitoring rule example: alert if a partner that normally sends 500 status updates an hour sends fewer than 50 in an hour during business hours.
pitfalls: Core services calling partner APIs directly.
No raw message archive, so bad files can't be reprocessed.
Monitoring only errors and missing silent outages.
No reconciliation, so lost messages are discovered by customers.

followups.q: A partner sends a file with a format change and half the records fail. What happens?
followups.a: Raw file archived, failures in the DLQ with alerts, adapter fixed, then the archived file replayed; the partner is contacted about the change.

followups.q: How do you onboard a new carrier quickly?
followups.a: Reuse standard adapters (EDI, common APIs) configured per partner, with a certification checklist and test messages.
Buy or use integration platforms for standard protocols like EDI and AS2; build adapters for strategic partners with custom APIs.

example: A logistics company found that 2% of shipments had never been acknowledged by one carrier, discovered only through customer complaints. An integration layer with per-carrier acknowledgement monitoring and daily reconciliation now catches such gaps within hours, and archived raw messages allow replay after fixes.
